source.cite: T.O. 33K3-4-2864-1, Calibration Procedure for Spectrum Analyzer 8591A (Hewlett-Packard), 30 May 2012
source.note: Points and limits are the document's own tables. Its measuring instruments (sweeper, power meter, counter, synthesizer, step attenuators, function and signal generators) are replaced by the Fluke 96270A (leveled sine, internal AM, NRP40T power-meter mode); each replacement is flagged UNVERIFIED on the point. The Calibration Performance Table is "Not Required". The self-calibration (3.3) and the display-line readings of 4.12 are prompts / typed readings.

discrepancies: Table 3 limits are 0.8 x the sweep time (8 modulation periods), but step 4.5.11 says the marker delta must be "on the eighth signal peak" (7 periods would be 0.7 x). The limits are used as printed; 8 periods are measured.
The -10 dB row (0 dBm applied) is printed in both Table 4 and Table 5 with the same limits; both are kept.
Table 1 lists a relative flatness of 1.0 dB; paragraph 4.11.31.4 gives 2.0 dB for the most positive minus the most negative value. 2.0 dB is used.
Table 1 gives the frequency reference aging for the standard unit as < 2 x 10^-6 per year; the paragraph limits 299.99925 to 300.00075 MHz are +/-2.5 ppm and are used as printed.

The document's measuring instruments are replaced by the 96270A (sweeper, power meter, counter, synthesizer, step attenuators, signal and function generators); see the flags. The 436A / 8481A power-meter step of 4.1 and 4.11 and the 3 dB attenuator of 4.1.2 have no equivalent here.
The 50 s and 100 s sweep-time rows need a 0.2 Hz and a 0.1 Hz modulation; the 96270A internal AM goes down to 1 Hz only (Operator Manual), so those two rows are listed as NOT TESTED.
Figures 1 to 4 are not reproduced; hook-up diagrams are supplied by the owner as PNG files in diagrams/ (hook_8591A_<GROUP>.png).

sections.title: Preliminary: analyzer self-calibration
sections.setup: Warm up 30 minutes, then run the analyzer's own self-calibration from its front panel (User's Guide, "Improving Accuracy With Self-Calibration Routines").

points.description: Self-calibration routines run after the 30 minute warm-up (1 = done)
flags: Prompt-based pass / fail: "the performance of the TI is only specified after the TI calibration routines have been run". The program never sends a calibration command to the analyzer (bench-first rule); you run the routines from the front panel and answer yes or no. The reading is 1 for done and 0 for not done.

points.description: CAL OUT amplitude, 300 MHz (-20 dBm)
flags: UNVERIFIED substitution: the document compares the CAL OUT peak with a synthesized sweeper through a 3 dB attenuator and then measures the SWEEPER with a 436A power meter + 8481A.
